info.name: TripPulse Jobs API
info.description:
Car rental job queue API with dual-pipeline scraping.

Flow:
1. POST /jobs/car-search → creates TWO async jobs:
   - car-search queue (Node.js) → mock + rentalcars API
   - car-scrape queue (Python)  → Hertz / Sixt / Enterprise via Playwright
2. Poll GET /jobs/:id until status = COMPLETED
3. GET /offers/cars?jobId=... → all offers from all sources

Notes:
- Prices are always in CENTS: 4500 = €45.00
- Node.js worker controls SearchJob status (PENDING→COMPLETED)
- Python scrapers add offers asynchronously — poll /offers/cars a few seconds after COMPLETED to see Hertz results
- providerName field identifies the source: "mock", "rentalcars", "hertz", "sixt", "enterprise"

variable.description: Python worker / Node worker metrics port

request.description:
Deep health check — probes PostgreSQL and Redis.
200 = healthy, 503 = degraded (at least one dependency down).

Prometheus text-format metrics from the API process.
Includes: http_requests_total, http_request_duration_ms, jobs_created_total.
See also Worker metrics on port 9091.

response.name: Prometheus text format
response.body:
# HELP http_requests_total Total HTTP requests
# TYPE http_requests_total counter
http_requests_total{method="GET",route="/health",status="200"} 3

# HELP jobs_created_total Total car search jobs created
# TYPE jobs_created_total counter
jobs_created_total{status="success"} 5
...

request.description:
Prometheus metrics from the Node.js worker process (port 9091).
Includes: job_processing_duration_ms, provider_call_duration_ms, provider_calls_total, jobs_active, jobs_processed_total.

response.name: Prometheus text format
response.body:
# HELP jobs_processed_total Total car search jobs processed by the worker
# TYPE jobs_processed_total counter
jobs_processed_total{status="COMPLETED"} 4
jobs_processed_total{status="PARTIAL"} 1

# HELP provider_calls_total Total provider search calls
# TYPE provider_calls_total counter
provider_calls_total{provider="mock",result="success"} 5
provider_calls_total{provider="rentalcars",result="failed"} 1

# HELP jobs_active Number of car search jobs currently being processed
# TYPE jobs_active gauge
jobs_active 0
...

exec: console.log('Both car-search (Node.js) and car-scrape (Python) jobs enqueued.');

request.description:
Creates a SearchJob and enqueues TWO async jobs:
1. car-search queue → Node.js worker (mock + rentalcars API)
2. car-scrape queue → Python worker (Hertz / Sixt / Enterprise via Playwright)

Returns 202 immediately. The test script saves jobId to {{jobId}}.

Tip: after COMPLETED, wait 2-3s and re-fetch /offers/cars — Hertz results may still be arriving.

item.name: Create car search job — validation error

request.description: Invalid pickupDateTime — should return 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

Poll this until status is COMPLETED, PARTIAL, or FAILED.

Status flow: PENDING → PROCESSING → COMPLETED | PARTIAL | FAILED

Note: COMPLETED means the Node.js pipeline finished.
The Python scraper (Hertz etc.) may still be running — check /offers/cars a few seconds later for additional results.

request.description:
Fetches paginated car offers for a completed job.
All query params except jobId are optional.

Prices are in cents: 4500 = €45.00

providerName values:
- "mock" — deterministic test data
- "rentalcars" — real API (requires RENTALCARS_API_KEY)
- "hertz" — Playwright scraper (real prices from hertz.com)
- "sixt" — Playwright scraper (skeleton, coming soon)
- "enterprise" — Playwright scraper (skeleton, coming soon)

Fetch 5 offers at a time. Check pagination.hasMore to know if there are more pages.
Should return 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. Valid types: economy, compact, midsize, suv, van, luxury.

Open Grafana in browser.
Login: admin / localdev

Dashboard 'TripPulse Jobs' shows:
- Jobs created/min
- Active jobs gauge
- Job processing time p50/p95
- Provider call latency per provider
- Provider success rate
- Worker logs (Loki)

Prometheus expression browser.
Sample queries:
  jobs_processed_total
  rate(provider_calls_total[5m])
  histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(job_processing_duration_ms_bucket[5m]))

Lightweight health check on the Node.js worker metrics server.
200 = worker process is alive.
